item.title: 49ers-Vikings roundtable: Mexico City showdown between two of NFC's best
item.description: Quarterback Brock Purdy and the 49ers offense have faced four defenses in the bottom six of the NFL this season - the Falcons, Cowboys, Cardinals and Raiders - possibly skewing their effectiveness. (Tony Gutierrez/Associated Press) The San Francisco 49ers have already delivered some big wins - the opener in Australia against the Rams and beating the Seahawks in Seattle among them - but suddenly their game in Mexico City against a really good Minnesota Vikings team might be their biggest test yet. Before the two teams tangle, we asked columnist Ann Killion and reporters Eric Branch and Harrison Rich for their answers to some key questions about the matchup. Have mounting injuries already ended the prime of Nick Bosa 's career? Is this his new normal in terms of production? Harrison Rich: Bosa has not looked like his old self since returning two weeks ago from a calf injury. He didn't look like himself earlier in the season, either, when he was dealing with knee tendinitis coming off his second torn right ACL. The 29-year-old defensive end hasn't recorded a sack in four games this season, his longest NFL drought. He pointed to two factors Wednesday for his struggles: He's still learning some of the quirks of defensive coordinator Raheem Morris' scheme, and he's still knocking off some rust. Bosa said he took "for granted" some of the things he used to be able to do automatically. Sunday's game, expected to have playoff-like intensity, will tell us a lot about the heights Bosa is still capable of reaching. Ann Killion: It's probably safe to say that Bosa will never again be the dominant force that he was in 2021 and 2022. Four years later, he's 29 and has a history of serious knee injuries. The fact that he thought, as he said this week, that he could "coast" and do the things he used to do "automatically" is an indication of just how hard it is for elite athletes to stay at that level, not only physically but mentally. Bosa's honest assessment this week means he will be even more in the spotlight in Sunday's game, where Minnesota's pass rush is expected to be the star. Eric Branch: It's a question Bosa might be asking himself. It was notable this week that Bosa admitted he was surprised he hasn't been able to return from last year's torn ACL and "automatically" perform at his All-Pro level. His extensive medical file includes three torn ACLs, two on the right knee he injured in 2025. Still, Bosa has shown some dominant flashes, such as when he hit Dak Prescott's arm in mid-throw last Sunday in Dallas after bullying right tackle Terence Steele with a bull rush. Also, Bosa has played in just four games this season, which qualifies as a small sample size. Verdict: It's premature to bury Bosa. item.title: Randy Flores brings a former player's perspective to Houston Astros GM job - and knows its limits
item.description: From player to scout to Astros GM, Randy Flores says firsthand experience helps him understand players - if he stays open to other perspectives. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) In his first year as St. Louis Cardinals scouting director , Randy Flores was watching a pitcher who threw a four-seam fastball and a curveball. The mix can be the backbone of a north-south pitching profile. But to Flores, a former major-league reliever, it looked suboptimal. "I'm like, ‘No, no, no - you sink it and slide it,'" said Flores, reciting an approach he gleaned from former Cardinals pitching coach Dave Duncan. As a slight left-hander who did not throw especially hard, Flores carved out a playing career that lasted parts of eight major-league seasons. So, his methods had merit. But as an executive now, he recalls the scouting anecdote as something of a cautionary tale. "Being a former player, if you're anchored too much to, ‘This is how it was done when I was playing,' it's the wrong thing," Flores said. Exploring other perspectives and means and finding a balance has been part of Flores' evolution as an executive, one that led to his hiring this month as general manager of the Houston Astros . It is also an arc to which only a handful of the majors' current highest-ranking baseball executives can relate. Of the current presidents of baseball operations, Jerry Dipoto (Mariners), Chris Young (Rangers), Craig Breslow (Red Sox) and Buster Posey (Giants) played in the majors. So did general managers Chris Getz (White Sox) and Flores, whom the Astros hired after 11-plus seasons in St. Louis' front office. That many top executives did not play in the majors, or at all professionally, illustrates how it is far from required. It might even invite the question of how such experience informs former players' approach to the role, if at all, as Flores settles into running a baseball operations department for the first time. "You probably have more empathy … for what a player goes through, from the moment they sign their first professional contract to when they get to the big leagues," Dipoto said at last week's GM meetings in Las Vegas. Dipoto and Breslow were relievers in the majors, like Flores. Dipoto posited that background could help "to understand the life of the guy who (is) not always the most thought-of player on the roster." "Outside of that, I think it's just business as usual," Dipoto said. "We each went through our own, I guess, apprenticeship (after playing). "You take the lessons you learn and apply them, just like any other general manager does when they get their first job. We just maybe have that slight - I don't even want to call it an advantage - that slight difference in that we have lived life in these players' shoes and probably as a result have a little bit more empathy rather than just frustration. item.title: Liverpool remain unsure over Virgil van Dijk contract decision
item.description: Liverpool remain unsure over Virgil van Dijk contract decision Virgil van Dijk contract latest as Liverpool weigh renewal and AC Milan interest Liverpool are facing a significant call on the future of Virgil van Dijk, with fresh reporting from Sport Italia indicating that the club remain hesitant over the defender’s preferred contract terms. Van Dijk, now 35, remains one of the defining figures of this Liverpool side. Even through major change, including the end of the Arne Slot era and the arrival of Andoni Iraola, his place in the team has carried real weight. His level, leadership and authority have kept him central to Liverpool’s defensive structure, while younger players around him continue to develop. The issue is not whether Van Dijk still contributes. By all accounts, he does. The issue is what Liverpool are prepared to commit to next, and on what financial and sporting terms. Sport Italia report outlines key Virgil van Dijk dilemma The update from Italy points to a familiar modern stand-off between club caution and player expectation. Sport Italia state, “Gerry Cardinale is following the Reds captain’s situation and dreams of a big signing this summer. The sticking point is a renewal: the Dutchman is asking for a two-year contract, while Liverpool still seem unconvinced.” That immediately places AC Milan into the conversation, albeit at a watching distance for now. The same report adds, “Virgil van Dijk’s future could become one of the most interesting situations of the upcoming summer transfer window. AC Milan is in the background, with Gerry Cardinale eyeing the possibility of bringing one of the most authoritative defenders in the international scene to San Siro.” There is still an important caveat. Liverpool hold the contract, and the club’s decision remains the key factor. As Sport Italia put it, “But before imagining the Dutch centre-back in a Rossoneri shirt, Liverpool must be taken into account.” That is where the matter sharpens. “This is precisely where the crux of the matter lies: Van Dijk wants a two-year extension, while Liverpool do not appear willing, at least for now, to fully grant his request.” Photo: IMAGO Liverpool contract policy under focus again This feels less about emotion and more about policy. Van Dijk is Liverpool’s highest-paid player, and by the start of next season he will be 36. Clubs at the elite end have to judge not only present performance, but the durability of that performance over the life of a deal. Even so, there is a strong football case for meeting him somewhere close to his request. Liverpool are still in a period of squad adjustment. Defensive planning matters, and certainty matters more. Van Dijk’s ongoing importance, on the pitch and inside the dressing room, means a short-term approach carries risk if there is no fully trusted successor ready to step in immediately. item.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Miami Heat turned a regular basketball game into a global video game launch. On Wednesday night, the Kaseya Center became the setting for the world premiere of Grand Theft Auto VI. This event blended the sport with gaming culture in a way few teams have ever tried. The arena makeover attracted a huge wave of fans who had never bought a ticket before. Hardwood floors and food stands transformed into spots from the new game. Lines for fictional eateries such as Burger Shot and Cluckin’ Bell were passed by walking fans. The attempt to make the entire structure resemble the game yielded immediate results. Local reporter Will Manso shared footage of packed concourse crowds, admitting he had never seen lines that long. According to Yahoo Sports , 95 percent of shoppers inside the team store were new. During their 137-130 win over the Milwaukee Bucks, Miami players sported special Vice City-themed jerseys. To align with the game’s style, the court displayed vibrant pink, blue, and black colors. The center court featured “Vice City” while the iconic “VI” logo was integrated into the design. This unique setup helped celebrate the long-awaited release of the sixth installment in the series. Merchandise sales exploded as fans rushed to own a piece of the night. Yahoo Sports reports that the black Court Culture “Vice City” Hoodie comes in adult sizes. Some items sold out fast, but five Vice-themed hats remain in stock online. item.title: England won't get carried away by All Blacks win
item.description: [BBC] In his latest BBC Sport column, England World Cup winner Matt Dawson reflects on Steve Borthwick's side's record win over New Zealand and previews the final round of Nations Championship fixtures. If England had produced that performance two years ago against New Zealand, there would have been a lap of honour and wild celebrations. Saturday felt like business. Job done, move on. And that is how it should be. It was a record victory for a northern hemisphere side against the All Blacks, yet at full-time you would hardly have known it. Even the post-match messaging from their leaders - Maro Itoje, Ellis Genge and Steve Borthwick - was that this performance had always been in them and that nobody was surprised. However, they will want to back it up. A tired but hurting New Zealand side will arrive at Allianz Stadium next Saturday looking for revenge. England beat the All Blacks in back-to-back Tests in 2002 and 2003. Matching that achievement on Saturday was a significant statement. Three consecutive wins over New Zealand, followed by a third-place finish, would leave England in a strong position heading into 2027, when the Rugby World Cup takes place in Australia. Lose, though, and it will be a waste of some great momentum. We have had many a false dawn with Borthwick's England, but something feels different this time. For me, that comes down to the players taking responsibility. Many of us ex-pros called for it during the Six Nations, and finally we are seeing the players take the lead on the style of rugby they want to play. It is an exciting, free-flowing brand of attacking rugby that mirrors what they are used to playing in the Prem. England's backs can compete with the very best and they tore through New Zealand on multiple occasions. Credit also has to go to Borthwick for allowing the players to take control. That, in itself, shows how he is learning and evolving as a head coach. Once players start getting 40, 50, 60 or 70 caps, they know more about certain aspects of the game than the coach because they are the ones out there experiencing it. If the environment does not allow players to turn around and say 'this isn't going to work', then it is never going to work. The reports before the Australia game suggested honest conversations took place, with the players wanting a greater say in how the team operates. The Six Nations was probably a big turning point. The change in mood and the feel-good factor are clear in the way England are carrying themselves. They now feel in control and, crucially, have a genuine sense of ownership in shaping the team and how it plays. 'An enormous statement about English rugby' Lewis Moody, a former team-mate of mine, joining the team to face the New Zealand haka was an enormous statement about English rugby. item.title: Chelsea boss Bompastor calls for better balance after draw at Liverpool
item.description: Chelsea boss Bompastor calls for better balance after draw at Liverpool Chelsea head coach Sonia Bompastor said that her her side need more balance between attack and defence after they drew 0-0 at Liverpool on Saturday afternoon. The Blues had chances to win the game, but they were unable to take full advantage as they dropped points in the title race. Speaking to the media after the match, Bompastor said that her side must have greater balance between defence and attack. “I’m really happy with a lot of things we are doing right now,” Bompastor said. “When you have ambitions, when you want to win titles, you need to make sure to find the right balance between being strong defensively, but also, being able to score goals. “I would like to have a better balance in terms of being able to score more.” Bompastor left it late to make attacking changes. Aggie Beever-Jones was not introduced until the 83rd minute. The Blues boss defended her decisions in the game. She said “I think all my decisions are based on performances. I think even if we were not able to score a goal in this game, what I was seeing on the pitch was good enough for me to still be confident. I think at this level, when you bring players even for 10, 12, 15 minutes, it’s enough for them to show and to prove, it didn’t happen today. I think the team [that] started was probably the team who was performing the best in training, games and everything.” Lola Brown made only her second WSL start and made a positive impact. Bompastor was full of praise for the youngster. She said “Lola hasn’t got many minutes because the competition is high in this squad, we have a lot of experienced players. item.title: ‘Embrace the love, America!’ – Young couple appear to break-up and make-up during Georgia Tech game
item.description: Photo by Eldon Lindsay/Georgia Tech Athletics/University Images via Getty Images Broadcast cameras caught a young couple at the Georgia Tech game having an argument, before later finding them having reconciled. College football games usually feature young fans in attendance trying increasingly bizarre tactics to try and get the attention of the TV cameras. However, one young couple at the Georgia Tech game would have hoped that their private interaction wouldn’t be broadcast on national television. Random college couple’s spat and reconciliation caught on ESPN cameras During Georgia Tech’s game against Wake Forest, ESPN cameras found a young couple sitting in the stands seemingly in the middle of an argument. While the broadcasters were speculating about the exchange, they did suggest that the pair were having an intense conversation, even using graphics to illustrate the nature of their conversation. Later in the game, the cameras panned back to the young couple, only to find them sharing an embrace having seemingly reconciled after the argument. “This is great! Embrace the love, America,” remarked the commentators when they were shown on the television feed. While the result on the field was not going Georgia Tech’s way, given that they were blown out 29-50 by Wake Forest, the young couple will be glad to have walked away from the game with their relationship intact. Unfortunately for them, their relationship became the subject of intense speculation on a national basis because of ESPN’s decision to aim their cameras on them while they were in the middle of a private conversation. Hopefully, they take the incident in their strides and don’t let the outside noise affect them and their relationship too much. (AP Photo/William Wotring) (William Wotring/Associated Press) MORGANTOWN, W.Va. - Top performers in No. 20 Houston's 34-31 victory over West Virginia : Keisean Henderson What a debut for the Cougars' quarterback of the future. Pressed into an emergency start with fifth-year senior Conner Weigman injured , Henderson directed two scoring drives in the final 5 ½ minutes as the Cougars rallied from a 10-point deficit to win on the road. The heralded freshman threw a touchdown on his first pass. He finished 18 of 28 for 268 yards against the Power Four's worst defense. "I wanted my teammates to know, and I was telling them on the sideline and letting them know that just because I'm a freshman, that doesn't mean I don't have a mindset to go out and win," Henderson said. Jonathan Dimas Dimas added another chapter to his clutch season, sealing the win with a 23-yard field goal as time expired. He also connected from 34 yards as he improved to 13-of-15 on field-goal attempts this season. His 54-yard attempt - which would have been a school record - hit the left upright. item.title: No. 5 Texas hosts Southern Indiana with plenty to improve upon
item.description: Dec 16, 2025; Austin, Texas, USA; Texas Longhorns head coach Sean Miller takes a time out during the second half against the Le Moyne Dolphins at Moody Center. There are plenty of coaching points for Texas to implement after Thursday’s disappointing 92-68 victory over Southern Utah that required the Longhorns to go on a late run to finally create separation after almost 30 minutes of disappointing basketball. Playing at a deliberate pace that put increased pressure on Texas to avoid late-clock fouls, defensive breakdowns, and giving up offensive rebounds, Southern Utah operated with a high level of efficiency in the first half and well into the second half, shooting 50 percent overall and 50 percent from three heading into halftime down just three points after leading by as many as nine points in the first half. “We had a hard time guarding them. item.title: Porto rally around defender that was left in tears by horror own goal
item.description: Porto have rallied around Francisco Moura after the player scored a horror own goal in his side’s Portuguese Cup tie on Friday, which reduced him to tears. The 27-year-old defender passed the ball into his own net in the 57th minute of the fourth-round tie against third-division side Paredes, inexplicably kicking it into the bottom left corner after a save by his goalkeeper. Moura dropped straight to the ground with his hands over his face, covering his head with his jersey as he started crying. He then signalled to the bench that he wanted to be substituted. Moura, who received support from both sets of players following the blunder, was not immediately substituted and later came off in the 70th minute. item.title: Manchester City's torrid winless run in the Premier League extended to four games on Saturday afternoon as yet another lacklustre display from Enzo Maresca's men saw the Blues draw 1-1 with Fulham at the Etihad Stadium.
item.description: Manchester City's torrid winless run in the Premier League extended to four games on Saturday afternoon as yet another lacklustre display from Enzo Maresca's men saw the Blues draw 1-1 with Fulham at the Etihad Stadium. How does Enzo Maresca fix Manchester City's defence? A City performace that was, for large parts, void of intensity and creativity, saw the Blues fail to beat Fulham at the Etihad Stadium for the first time in 15 years, dating back to February 2011 under Roberto Mancini. There was hope that, after the international break, those of a sky-blue persuasion would be galvanised to right the wrongs of their recent shortcomings, having suffered three consecutive league defeats; unfortunately, however, it was more of the slothful same. In the opening exchanges, Maresca's men struggled to ride the storm of Fulham 's intensity but did conjure some somewhat presentable chances early on, with Erling Haaland seeing his effort thwarted by David Affengruber whilst a deflection steered Nico O'Reilly's shot narrowly wide. However, with just 16 minutes on the clock, Manchester City 's defensive frailties reared their ugly head once again as the Cottagers drew first blood in the tie through Rodrigo Muniz, who latched on to a superb pass from former Blue Oscar Bobb and hammered past Gianluigi Donnarumma to give the visitors the lead. Just eight minutes later, the home side thought they had restored parity after an excellent cross from Iliman Ndiaye found Haaland, and the 26-year-old, after squandering the initial chance, seized upon a goalkeeping mishap by Bernd Leno, prodding home after the German appeared to spill the ball. But referee Thomas Bramall, controversially brought the celebrations to an abrupt halt, having adjudged that the former Arsenal shot-stopper had two hands on the ball at the time of the Norwegian's follow-up, resulting in a foul and disallowed goal. Subsequently, a defensive blunder from O'Reilly nearly proved calamitous as the Englishman allowed Bobb to snatch possession inside the Manchester City area, but Donnarumma was on hand to spare his teammate's blushes and deny the Fulham number 14. After a dismal first 45 which saw the halftime whistle met with jeers from the Etihad Stadium crowd, Maresca was in dire need of an injection of impetus into his side, and 12 minutes after the restart, Elliott Anderson obliged, producing a sumptuous volley which nestled into the back of the Fulham net and hauled the hosts level. Whilst the goal certainly did breathe some life into the home side, City were still by no means at their scintillating best in the second period, with the lack of ideas and desire remaining a glaringly obvious issue. In truth, Fulham looked more likely to walk away with three points, but Donnarumma, whose shot-stopping was much improved, remained resolute, preventing both Muniz and Calvin Bassey from deciding the tie late on. item.description: Matt Campbell During a Press Conference © Imagn Penn State head coach Matt Campbell was put on the hot seat by Barstool Sports’ Brandon Walker following the Nittany Lions’ 25-24 loss to Rutgers on Saturday. The Nittany Lions entered the matchup as clear favorites against a Rutgers team that had won just two games all season. However, the Scarlet Knights ultimately blew Penn State’s two-score lead. After the game, Walker called out Campbell for the loss against Rutgers, deeming it a fireable offense. “I honestly think that might be a fireable offense for Matt Campbell at Penn State. You can’t ever lose to Rutgers,” Walker wrote on X. Penn State had led 16-0 and later held a 24-10 advantage with less than 11 minutes remaining. Rutgers pulled off a stunning comeback. Rutgers running back Antwan Raymond caught a pass short of the goal line and lateraled to wide receiver Ben Black III, who scored on the final play of regulation. Rutgers converted the ensuing two-point attempt to take a 25-24 lead. Time ran out before Penn State could reply. The loss against Rutgers was particularly damaging because it ended Penn State’s 18-game winning streak against the Scarlet Knights. Penn State last lost in 1988. HC Matt Campbell Takes Responsibility for Penn State’s Collapse In his post-game conference, Penn State head coach Matt Campbell took responsibility for the loss to Rutgers. “I didn’t have us prepared to play our best football game, Senior Day, the end of the season, and that really hurts me, and it puts a lot of responsibility on my shoulders,” Campbell said via Go PSU Sports. “To me, our ability to do hard things is still keeping this team from becoming its best.” Campbell added that the team has failed to be excellent for the full 60 minutes, leading to poor finishes in several games. Previously, the Nittany Lions failed to close the game against Wisconsin. On Saturday, they allowed Rutgers 15 unanswered points. Penn State quarterback Rocco Becht and running back Cam Wallace committed two costly fumbles in the loss. As a result, the Nittany Lions could only manage 26 yards of offense in the fourth quarter. Penn State entered the matchup against Rutgers after recording three straight wins. They had the momentum and were making progress under Campbell before the latest heartbreaking loss. Penn State fell to 6-5 overall and 3-5 in Big Ten play. The Nittany Lions will conclude their regular season against Maryland on November 28. item.title: Mikel Arteta confirms major Arsenal injury blow after Newcastle United clash
item.description: Mikel Arteta confirms major Arsenal injury blow after Newcastle United clash David Raya Injury Concern Clouds Arsenal After Newcastle Draw Arsenal left St James’ Park with a point, but the bigger issue is in goal. David Raya, one of the key reasons behind Arsenal’s strong opening to the season, went off injured in the 2-2 draw with Newcastle and now faces scans on a suspected shoulder problem. The sequence was straightforward enough. Raya collided with William Osula while trying to release the ball, went down in clear discomfort and needed treatment on the pitch. He could not continue. He walked off, headed straight down the tunnel and that will worry Arsenal far more than the dropped points. There is no need to dress it up. If Raya is out, it is a problem. He has been reliable, calm and productive, with seven clean sheets in Arsenal’s first ten Premier League games. That sort of consistency matters, particularly for a side heading into a run that can shape its season. Photo IMAGO Mikel Arteta Awaits David Raya Scan Results Mikel Arteta offered no certainty after the match, saying: “Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is not good news. “He will have an MRI assessment tomorrow, but at the moment I don’t know.” He added: “It was a knock, I don’t know how it happened and what the injury is at the moment. We have to wait and see tomorrow. “We know how important David is for us. Tomorrow we will have more news.” Arsenal Fixtures Make Raya Injury More Serious Kepa Arrizabalaga replaced Raya for the final 20 minutes, entering with Arsenal 2-1 down. By full-time it had finished 2-2, though the result quickly became secondary. Arsenal had led at the break through Eberechi Eze, then lost control after half-time as Newcastle turned the game. Now comes the difficult part. Arsenal host Manchester City next weekend, with Real Madrid, Tottenham and Manchester United also on the schedule before Christmas. If Raya misses any part of that spell, Arsenal’s margin for error shrinks. There is enough quality in the squad, but goalkeeper injuries are different. You do not rotate calm, command and trust so easily.

item.title: Watford sack boss Dionisi after 18 games
item.description: Alessio Dionisi was the fifth Italian manager hired by Watford under the ownership of the Pozzo family [Getty Images] Watford are looking for their sixth manager in 18 months after they sacked head coach Alessio Dionisi following 18 games in charge. The 46-year-old Italian was appointed in June after the departure of Ed Still, who himself lasted only three months at Vicarage Road. Still, Javi Gracia and Paulo Pezzolano were all also given full-time contracts after Tom Cleverley left in May 2025. Dionisi was Watford's 12th head coach, not including interim bosses, since the end of the 2020-21 season, and leaves the Hornets searching for a 25th since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012. The club have had 57 permanent managers in their 145-year history. The decision to replace him comes after Saturday's crushing 4-0 defeat by Sheffield United at Bramall Lane. Dionisi's dismissal caps an underwhelming start to the season, with the Hornets having won just four league games to leave them 21st in the table. "We thank Alessio and his staff for his professionalism and their efforts," sporting director Luke Dowling told the club website. "As I'm sure the supporters have seen, Alessio is a really good guy and we wish him the best for the future. "The process has started for a replacement and we hope to be in a position to announce that shortly." Dionisi was sacked by Serie B club Empoli in March after only five months in charge following a run of five wins in 22 matches. His spell in charge of the Hornets was his first outside his homeland and started promisingly when his youthful side beat Southampton in their opening league game. But they won only two of their next 12 in all competitions, and despite deservedly beating Charlton on 17 October, reverses at Wolves and Norwich followed, before four points from Dionisi's final three games in charge of the Hertfordshire side and his dismissal means further upheaval for the Hornets. With more than a third of the league season complete, Watford are one place outside of the Championship relegation zone (table shown before Burnley face Blackburn on Sunday) [BBC] Since sacking Cleverley at the end of the 2024-25 campaign, the club has now been through four permanent head coaches, as well as interim boss Charlie Daniels' two-game spell in charge. Of those four, only Gracia, in his second spell at Vicarage Road, took charge of more than 20 games. On the morning of their final-day drubbing by Coventry last season, chief executive Scott Duxbury wrote a statement on the club website saying Watford had made mistakes, labelling their end to the campaign "unacceptable" and "truly disappointing in the extreme". Their triumph in Barranquilla ended an 18-year continental wait for the club. Paredes celebrates as Riquelme claims first title Boca Juniors defeated Atletico Mineiro 2-0 at the Estadio Metropolitano Roberto Melendez in Barranquilla to become the first three-time Copa Sudamericana champions. Santiago Ascacibar opened the scoring in the 16th minute before Miguel Merentiel struck three minutes into the second half. item.title: Gameday column: Bills and the current state of strength of schedule
item.description: It’s like each week there’s arisen a new narrative about this Buffalo Bills team. Leading into Week 11 against the Dolphins, it was all about strength of schedule… probably because of Buffalo’s competition — or lack thereof — since the bye week. I’ll be the first to mention that teams are not always what their record says they are. But what these Bills are doing is subtly different from previous Bills teams during the Josh Allen era. What has remained the same is Buffalo’s regular-season dominance. Since 2020, the Bills have been the NFL’s best team in the regular season. They have the most wins and the highest point differential by an insane margin. But like I wrote a week ago, the Sean McDermott clubs always had an uncharacteristic stumble or two during said regular season that kept them away out of the No. 1 seat in the AFC playoffs. Of course today, against the Dolphins, represents one of those “stumble” possibilities with the colossal clash on Thanksgiving against the Chiefs looming. But that’s the not the crux of this column. Are the Bills the best 8-1 team in NFL history? No. Are they the best 8-1 team in the past decade. No. But they’ve done exactly what a team should do against the competition level it has faced. Regarding the aforementioned point differential, it’s my absolute favorite measure of team quality… because it’s straightforward and pretty darn predictive. How’s this for point differential’s stickiness — 11 of the past 12 Super Bowl winners finished the regular season in the Top 6 in point differential. Insane, right? From 2004 – 2025, 17 of 22 of the clubs that hoisted the Lombardi Trophy at season’s end were a Top 6 point-differential team during the regular season. And this Bills team enters this AFC East game against the Dolphins second in point differential, at +88. If Buffalo had been squeaking by lesser opponents regularly, I’d be the first to write their 8-1 feels phony. That hasn’t been the case whatsoever. And teams can only play the opponents on their schedule. Among the nine teams at 7-2 or better right now, only the Broncos (.583) and Vikings (.518) have faced a cumulative opponent win percentage above .500. The Bills are third on that list at .480, as their opponents have a combined record of 40-47. The combined record of Chiefs’ opponents to date is 34-53 (.391). They’re currently in last in that metric. (another shoutout to Jeremy White from WGR550 who noticed this earlier this week.) Oh, and as for the strength-of-schedule element that legitimately matters come playoff-seeding time — the Bills currently have the second-best strength of victory at .455, behind only the Broncos, the sole AFC club with a strength of victory over .500. On this note, the first half of the 2026 NFL season has shown a more sizable gap between the great teams and the noticeably bad ones. item.title: How Lee Trevino reacted to Phil Mickelson’s scathing criticism of Tom Watson after the 2014 Ryder Cup
item.description: Photo by BEN STANSALL / AFP via Getty Images Phil Mickelson caused uproar in 2014 after he very publicly criticized the 2014 US Ryder Cup captain, Tom Watson. Mickelson has always been regarded as one of the most outspoken players on the professional golfing scene. And he certainly lived up to his reputation back in 2014 after the United States were comfortably beaten by Team Europe at the Ryder Cup. During the press conference after the United States’ Ryder Cup defeat to Europe, Phil Mickelson was asked to put his finger on what went wrong at Gleneagles. The now 56-year-old took a swipe at Tom Watson ‘s refusal to stick to Paul Azinger’s ‘pod system’ that worked to excellent effect during the 2008 Ryder Cup at Valhalla. “ There were two things that allow us to play our best, I think, that Paul Azinger did, and one was he got everybody invested in the process, “ Mickelson explained. “ He got everybody invested in who they were going to play with, who the picks were going to be, who was going to be in their pod, who — when they would play, and they had a great leader for each pod. In my case, we had Ray Floyd, and we hung out together and we were all invested in each other’s play. We were invested in picking Hunter that week; Anthony Kim and myself and Justin were in a pod, and we were involved on having Hunter be our guy to fill our pod. So we were invested in the process. “ And the other thing that Paul did really well was he had a great game plan for us, you know, how we were going to go about doing this. How we were going to go about playing together; golf ball, format, what we were going to do, if so-and-so is playing well, if so-and-so is not playing well, we had a real game plan. Those two things helped us bring out our best golf. “ We use that same process in The Presidents Cup and we do really well. Unfortunately, we have strayed from a winning formula in 2008 for the last three Ryder Cups, and we need to consider maybe getting back to that formula that helped us play our best. “ Mickelson’s comments drew audible gasps from the press room and the tension in the room was palpable. The six-time major champion had just openly criticized the captaincy methods of one of the greatest golfers ever to have played the game. item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports The Miami Dolphins are not a pushover just because they sit at one win and eight losses. Josh Allen knows this better than anyone. He told his teammates to watch the tape closely because the defense is doing fantastic things. The numbers back up his warning. A team that stops the pass that well can make life miserable for any quarterback. Allen has faced Miami many times before. He owns a 14-3 career record against them. But the history lesson might not help him this time. He called the unit “very sticky” and praised the head coach for keeping the scheme in sync. The offense is ready to light up the scoreboard. But the defense has to match that energy. The Dolphins defense has been their saving grace. Ranked 10th in the NFL for total yards allowed, they average 320.6 yards per contest. Although facing difficulties in other areas, this ranking puts them within the top third of the league. item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team.
